title: Authored lines for the Oracle cells
label: invention
$comment: The book defines none of the Oracle's cell words - 'No, and', 'Disaster', 'Territorial', 'Special', 'Ambush' - and the estate found no defensible inference for them (row A37). Interpretation stays the player's; these are the lines this build reads aloud when a cell comes up, so a solo table has a sentence rather than a word. The word itself stays verbatim in oracle.json. Cells that print the same word (Outcome 2 and 3, for instance) still get their own line: the die distinguishes them even where the table does not.

records.line: No, and the asking has cost you something you had not counted.
No. Plainly, and with nothing offered in its place.
No, but the door it closes was not the only door.
Yes, but the yes arrives with a condition you did not set.
Yes. Take it and move.
Yes, and more than you asked for comes with it.
It goes wrong in the way you were not watching for, and the wrongness spreads.
It falls short. Not ruin, but you are further from where you meant to be.
It sours late, after you had already begun to count on it.
It works, roughly, and the roughness will not matter.
It works cleanly, and someone notices that it did.
It works better than the attempt deserved, and the room changes shape around it.
They have already decided about you, and the decision was not kind.
They keep the table between you and answer only what is asked.
They have not seen you yet. Whatever happens next is entirely your choice.
They make room, and the making of room is genuine.
They put down what they were doing and ask what you need.
They go, quickly, and they do not look back to see whether you follow.
It comes for you without preamble; there was never a moment to defuse.
It holds its ground and makes the boundary obvious. Cross it and this changes.
It has not registered you. The wind is in your favour, for now.
It comes closer than it should, interested rather than hungry.
It suffers your presence, and would suffer your hand on it.
It breaks and runs, and the noise of its going tells everything nearby that you are here.
They were waiting. The first exchange happens before you know there is one.
They come at you openly, and there is no version of this that is not a fight.
No greeting, no demand. They close the distance and that is the whole of it.
Weapons come out on their side first, and yours follow because they must.
Nobody swings. What happens next depends on how they read you.
The meeting stays a meeting. Find out what they are.
Numbers, not skill. Individually they are nothing; that is not the problem.
Someone who takes orders and is competent at taking them.
A trusted hand, sent because the matter was worth sending a trusted hand.
A fighter by trade, who has done this often enough to be calm about it.
Real training behind the stance. This one will cost you.
The one the others answer to, and the one who chose that you would meet.
Roll, and accept the number. It could be one; it could be a room full.
Three of them, spread wide enough that you cannot watch all three.
Three, and they have done this together before.
Two, which is one more than you can face cleanly.
Two, and the second one is holding back to see how you move.
One. Whatever else is true, this is between the two of you.
Straightforward, and no less dangerous for it.
They fight the way they were taught, without flourish.
Nothing you have not seen. Everything you have seen still works.
They open with something you did not know they had.
The style shows itself, and the style is the point.
They stop holding back the thing they were holding back.
It stands open, which is either luck or an invitation.
Ajar, and nobody thought it worth closing behind them.
Open, and the dust on the sill says it has been for a while.
It opens. Something else opens with it.
Locked, and the lock was chosen by someone who expected you.
Shut, unlocked, and heavier than it looks.
That was the last of it. Whatever you were relying on, stop.
One left, and after it you are asking someone for more.
Enough for once more, and not for the once after that.
More than you need, which means you can be careless with it. Once.
Plenty. This is not the thing that will run out on you.
A supply, and the question becomes how much of it you can carry.
Worth having, not worth arguing over.
The price of a night indoors and a meal you did not cook.
Enough to matter to someone poor, and to be noticed if you spend it fast.
Real money. Somebody has already missed it.
The kind of sum that buys silence, or ends it.
A fortune, and a fortune is a reason for the next three people you meet.
